# TiffinDB v1 build: context brief

Condensed from `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/plan.md` (draft 5), `docs/ui-design-plan.md` (draft 1), ADRs 0001 to 0007, `docs/design/model-ui/README.md`, `docs/design/tokens.css`, `docs/brand/README.md`. References: "plan N" = `docs/plan.md` section N; "ui N" = `docs/ui-design-plan.md` section N; "ADR n"; "CLAUDE" = `CLAUDE.md`. "Not specified" means the source documents are silent. Section 12 lists contradictions and gaps; they are flagged, not resolved.

Precedence: CLAUDE (highest) > ADRs and plan (behaviour) > ui plan (appearance) (ui 1). Status of sources: planning; no application code exists. New decisions must be recorded in `docs/decisions/` before scaffolding (CLAUDE, Project).

Naming note: this brief omits company names. "The reference shared host" is the host named in plan 2 row 13 and CLAUDE "Platform targets".

## 1. Architecture

Stack (ADR 0001, plan 2): PHP 8.3+, no framework, Apache with `.htaccess`, server-rendered HTML, vanilla JS as progressive enhancement only, no build step. SQLite via PDO. MySQL/MariaDB not required. English only in v1; all UI strings in one strings file (plan 2 row 11, ui 10). Design priorities in order: ease of use, legibility/accessibility, data ownership/portability, simple shared-host install, plugin extensibility (plan 1).

### 1.1 Layers (plan 3.1)

| Layer | Responsibility | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| `core/storage` | SQLite access (PDO), transactions, project open/create, attachments on disk | none |
| `core/schema` | Tables, fields, field types, relations, user-schema migrations | storage |
| `core/query` | Record CRUD, search, sort, filter, saved collections | schema, storage |
| `core/io` | Importer/exporter interfaces, neutral intermediate model, plugin discovery | schema, query |
| `core/forms` | Form generation from schema, form HTML sanitizer, binding records to form HTML | schema |
| `core/auth` | Users, sessions, roles, project grants, CSRF | "system DB" |
| `web/` | Routing, controllers, templates, static assets | all core |
| `plugins/` | Import, export, later field-type plugins | `core/io` interfaces |
| `mcp/` (post-v1) | MCP endpoint and OAuth; adapter over core only | all core |

Binding constraints from M1 (plan 8 last paragraph, ADR 0005 consequences):
- Every operation is callable through `core/` without the web layer; no logic may live only in `web/` controllers.
- Authorization checks live in core, not in controllers.
- Record trash, project snapshots, and an audit log are core features.
- Core must be testable headlessly (plan 3.1, CLAUDE Working Conventions); data model, storage, query, import/export separated from presentation.
- Importers never write to storage directly; they produce the neutral intermediate model; exporters consume the same model (plan 6.1).

### 1.2 On-disk layout (plan 3.2, marked "proposed")

```
tiffindb/
  public/      web root: index.php, .htaccess, assets/ (css, js, fonts)
  src/         core and web PHP (not web-reachable)
  plugins/     import/csv/ import/xlsx/ import/bento/  export/csv/ export/xlsx/ export/json/
  vendor/      Composer dependencies, shipped in the release archive
  data/        git-ignored; not web-reachable
    system.sqlite
    projects/<project-id>/
      project.tiffin   SQLite database
      attachments/     content-addressed files
      snapshots/       automatic copies before migrations and other risky operations
```

Fonts are served from `public/assets/fonts/` with each family's licence file (ui 10). How layer names (`core/schema`, `web/`, `mcp/`) map to paths under `src/` is not specified.

## 2. Data formats

### 2.1 Project database (ADR 0001, plan 3.3)

- One SQLite file `project.tiffin` per project, in a per-project folder that also holds attachments. A project is a folder, transferable as a zip archive (ADR 0004). Backup is a folder copy (ADR 0001).
- Each user table is a real SQLite table with real typed columns (not EAV), so the file is usable with any SQLite tool.
- Metadata is in reserved `_tiffin_*` tables in the same file:

| Table | Content (plan 3.3) |
|---|---|
| `_tiffin_meta` | Format version, project name, creation info |
| `_tiffin_tables` | User tables: stable key, display name, order |
| `_tiffin_fields` | Fields: stable key, display name, type, options (JSON), order |
| `_tiffin_relations` | Link definitions between tables; many-to-many via generated join tables |
| `_tiffin_forms` | Form HTML, CSS, target table, default flag |
| `_tiffin_collections` | Saved filters/sorts (smart collections) |
| `_tiffin_attachments` | File hash, original name, MIME type, size |
| `_tiffin_import_log` | Source, plugin, time, row counts, warnings |

- Column lists, column types, and key formats for these tables: not specified beyond the above.
- Identifier rule (plan 7): table and column names are generated by the application, never taken from user text. The generation scheme and the format of "stable key" are not specified.
- Format must be documented in `docs/formats/tiffin.md` and versioned. Upgrades are forward-only migrations with an automatic file copy beforehand (plan 3.3).
- Join tables and referential cleanup are part of the schema engine from the start (ADR 0004).
- Concurrency: WAL mode where the filesystem supports it, busy timeout, short transactions; household scale assumed (plan 10).

### 2.2 Forms in the project file (ADR 0003, ADR 0006, plan 4)

- A form = HTML fragment + scoped CSS block. Binding attribute working name `data-tiffin-field="<field key>"`; the server fills values and emits the input control for the field type. No per-form JavaScript; forms work without JS.
- Form source lives only in the project database (no on-disk mirror); Admin download/upload as a file.
- The v1 format must already support (ADR 0006 "Consequences for v1"): explicit grid placement (column, row, span) on any element; static unbound elements (headings, text blocks, dividers, images); a format version marker in each stored form; sanitizer rules covering these from the start. The attribute vocabulary is part of the documented project format and must be versioned (ADR 0003).
- Auto-generation (plan 4): one accessible single-column layout per table (label + control pairs, `fieldset` grouping, relation lists at the end); runs on table creation and after import.
- Simple editor (Admin only): reorder, show/hide, width on a CSS grid, group under headings, rename labels; reads and writes the same HTML/CSS. Source view with validation.
- Form CSS is restricted to layout and design tokens; may reference tokens but not redefine them (plan 4, ui 10). User accessibility settings override form CSS.

### 2.3 Attachments (ADR 0004, plan 3.2, 3.3, 7)

Stored in `attachments/` beside the SQLite file, content-addressed; metadata in `_tiffin_attachments`. Served only through an access-checked endpoint with safe content types and `Content-Disposition`. Upload type and size limits, MIME checks, and storage quotas "need handling" (ADR 0004). Hash algorithm, directory fan-out, limit values, quota values, and orphan cleanup: not specified.

### 2.4 Snapshots, trash, audit log

| Feature | What the docs say | Not specified |
|---|---|---|
| Snapshots | `snapshots/` in the project folder: "automatic copies before migrations and other risky operations" (plan 3.2); automatic file copy before format upgrades (plan 3.3); core feature from M1 (plan 8); post-v1: snapshot before any MCP schema change or import (ADR 0005) | Naming, retention, restore UI, which v1 operations count as "risky" |
| Trash | Trash with restore for records; no per-record change history in v1 (plan 2 row 12); core feature from M1 (plan 8); UI label "Move to trash"; Trash in sidebar (ui 5) | Storage mechanism (no `_tiffin_*` table or column listed), whether tables/fields/projects can be trashed, who may restore |
| Audit log | Core feature required from M1 (plan 8, ADR 0005). Post-v1: every MCP call logged with client, user, tool, target; visible to Admins | Location (system DB or project file), schema, which v1 events are logged, v1 UI |

### 2.5 System database (ADR 0001, 0002, 0007; ui 8)

`data/system.sqlite`: users, sessions, project registry, access grants. The grant table must carry a level column from the start (read-only level is a likely later addition) (ADR 0002). Per-user appearance settings are stored server-side in the system database; the user settings table needs `typeface` and `accent` columns in addition to theme, text size, line spacing, reduced motion (ADR 0007, ui 8). Table names and column lists: not specified.

### 2.6 Accounts and roles (ADR 0002)

Individual logins. Admin: manages users, projects, imports/exports, plugins, schema, form design. Member: views and edits records in projects they have been granted. Access is granted per user per project. Members cannot edit forms (plan 4).

## 3. Field types (plan 3.4, "v1 candidate set")

Text, long text, number, currency, date, time, date-time, duration, checkbox, choice (single), rating, URL, email, phone, attachment (file/image), relation, auto-number (17 types).

Deferred: calculated fields, multi-choice, address composite, encrypted fields.

Each type defines: storage column type, validation, HTML input rendering, display rendering, import coercion, export formatting. All types sit behind one interface so they can later become plugins.

Per-type notes found in the docs (everything else per type is not specified):

| Type | Note | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Relation | First-class in v1; imports preserve relations; forms show related records; users add and remove links; many-to-many via generated join tables | ADR 0004, plan 3.3 |
| Attachment | File and image; see 2.3 | ADR 0004 |
| Rating | Component is a radio group 1 to 5 with end labels | ui 7 |
| Number | Right-aligned in data tables | ui 7 |
| Date | Native input; JS date picker only "where native ones are weak" | plan 4 |
| Unsupported source types (legacy import) | Imported as text where possible, always listed in the import report | plan 6.4 |

## 4. Security baseline (plan 7 unless noted)

| Area | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Passwords | `password_hash`: Argon2id where available, bcrypt otherwise |
| Sessions | Cookies `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` on HTTPS |
| CSRF | Tokens on all state-changing requests (owned by `core/auth`) |
| SQL | Prepared statements only; identifiers generated by the application, never from user text |
| CSP | Strict Content-Security-Policy, no inline script; no inline `style` attributes or inline scripts in application output (ui 10). Exact policy string not specified |
| Form sanitizer | Allowlist: no `script`, no event-handler attributes, no external URLs, no `style` escapes out of the form scope (plan 4); must cover grid placement and static elements (ADR 0006). CSP backs it up. Admin-only editing bounds the risk (ADR 0002) |
| Attachments | Access-checked endpoint only; safe content types and `Content-Disposition`; upload type and size limits; MIME checks (ADR 0004) |
| Data directory | Installer must (a) prefer `data/` outside the web root, (b) otherwise write a deny-all `.htaccess` into `data/`, (c) test over HTTP that `data/` is unreachable and refuse to finish setup if it is reachable (plan 3.2, ADR 0001, plan 10) |
| Installer checks | Requirement check for `pdo_sqlite`, `zip`, `xmlreader` with plain-language messages (plan 10) |
| Network | No telemetry, no outbound network calls (plan 7, CLAUDE). No network font loading (plan 5) |
| AGPL s.13 | "Source code" link in footer or About page; ui 5 puts licence line and link in the footer of every screen including sign-in |
| Plugins | Run with full PHP privileges, no sandbox; only Admins install; must be stated plainly in documentation (plan 6.2) |
| Authorization | Checks in core, not controllers (plan 8) |
| Post-v1 MCP | Disabled by default; OAuth 2.1; scopes `read`/`write`/`schema`; role ceiling; per-project consent; no permanent deletion; snapshots; audit log; revocation; rate and size limits; `.htaccess` must pass the `Authorization` header and the installer must test it (ADR 0005) |

Not specified: password policy, login throttling/lockout, session lifetime and storage details, password reset mechanism, security headers other than CSP.

## 5. Accessibility and visual system (plan 5, ui 3, 4, 8, tokens.css)

- WCAG 2.2 AA throughout; default theme aims for 7:1 text contrast. Usable at 200% and 400% zoom without horizontal scrolling of forms; tables scroll inside their own box. Full keyboard operation, visible focus, landmarks, labels on every control, errors tied to fields. Touch targets min 44 px, form inputs 48 px. Plain-language text ("Bring in", "Move to trash", "Space between lines").
- One primary (filled) action per screen; words before icons; reading order equals visual order (ui 3).
- Automated checks in the test suite: static HTML validation and contrast tests on tokens; manual screen-reader pass per milestone (plan 5).
- Appearance settings are per user, server-side, applied as root-element classes, working without JS (ui 8):

| Setting | Values (default first) | Root class |
|---|---|---|
| Theme | light, dark, high-contrast light, high-contrast dark | none, `t-dark`, `t-hcl`, `t-hcd` |
| Accent | teal, indigo, plum, graphite | none, `a-indigo`, `a-plum`, `a-graphite`; server omits it in high-contrast themes |
| Typeface | Inter, Atkinson Hyperlegible, Lexend, Source Serif 4, device sans, device serif | none, `f-atk`, `f-lexend`, `f-serif4`, `f-sans`, `f-serif` |
| Text size | standard 18 px; small 16, large 21, larger 24, largest 28 | root font size; all sizes in `rem` (not CSS `zoom`) |
| Line spacing | standard 1.5; roomy 1.75; very roomy 2 | root line height |
| Reduce movement | off; on whenever the device asks for reduced motion | disables transitions |

- Tokens: start the application stylesheet from `docs/design/tokens.css` (copy values; token names `--bg --surface --sunk --ink --ink2 --line --ctl --accent --on-accent --soft --warn --warn-soft --brand2 --side*`). Shape: radius 8 px controls, 12 px cards, pill for top-bar items and current sidebar item; borders 2 px controls, 1 px cards; focus 3 px accent outline with 2 px offset on every focusable element; spacing steps 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48 px; content widths forms 800 px (1120 px in columns), settings and import 1120 px (ui 4.4).
- Fixed type roles at Standard: page title 34 px, section title 22 px, small text 16 px. Weights 400 and 700 only (ui 4.3).
- Shell (ui 5): top bar 68 px (mark + wordmark linking to project list; project search on list view or Admin tabs on project list; Display link, user chip with initials, Sign out); colour-blocked sidebar on list view (project name, "Switch project", Tables with counts, Collections with counts and "New collection", Import/Export/Trash pinned at bottom; stacks above content when narrow); breadcrumb Project / Table / Item on record, collection, import screens; footer on every screen.
- Components to build once as server-side partials plus classes (ui 7): button (primary, secondary, destructive, disabled), link variants, inputs with label above/help below/error tied, checkbox and radio (24 px control in 44 px row; radio card), rating, relation field, file row, linked-record row, fieldset card, data table, step indicator, notice, shell parts.
- Brand (brand README): top-bar mark is inline SVG using `currentColor`, following the theme accent; wordmark is live text in Atkinson Hyperlegible Bold, tracking -0.025 em, regardless of user typeface, never re-set in Inter; favicon `docs/brand/tiffindb-mark-small.svg`; sign-in shows the larger horizontal lockup. Do not stretch, recolour tiers, add effects, or combine with other logos. No text in Turmeric `#C27F00` on light grounds (3.32:1).
- Designed mock-ups (ui 6.1): `sign-in.html` (M1), `projects.html` (M1), `list.html` (M2), `record.html` (M2, M4), `collection.html` (M4), `import.html` (M3), `settings.html` (M2). Mock-ups are not application code: they use inline styles, CSS `zoom`, and network fonts, none of which may be carried over. `corners`, `sidebar`, `rows` preview options are explorations, not user settings.

## 6. Import and export (plan 6, ADR 0004)

- Pipeline (plan 6.1): file -> `Importer.inspect()` -> proposed schema + preview -> user review (rename fields, change types, pick target table, skip columns) -> `Importer.read()` rows -> coercion -> single transaction commit -> import report (counts, warnings, skipped values) -> auto-generated form.
- Neutral intermediate model: tables, typed fields, row iterator, relations, attachment streams.
- Plugin contract (plan 6.2, "sketch"): a directory with a manifest (id, name, version, kind, file extensions, license) and a class implementing `Importer` or `Exporter`; discovery by directory scan; Admin can enable/disable.

| Format | Direction | Notes (plan 6.3) |
|---|---|---|
| CSV | import, export | Delimiter/encoding detection, header row option, type inference, streaming |
| XLSX | import, export | One table per sheet; streaming library for shared-host memory limits |
| JSON | export | Full project, schema included; documented in `docs/formats/` |
| Bento | import | Clean-room; see below |
| Project archive | export, import | Zip of the project folder; native backup/transfer path |

Legacy-product import (plan 6.4): source file form unknown; discovery is the first task. Unverified assumptions: desktop package contains a SQLite store openable read-only with `pdo_sqlite`; template exports may embed a similar structure. Rules: clean-room from observation of legitimately owned files only; real files never enter the repo, issues, or commit messages; discovery runs locally outside the working tree; discovery script emits structure only (table names, column names and types, row counts), and even that output needs maintainer review before commit; fixtures are SQLite files generated by a seeded script reproducing the observed structure with synthetic records. Findings go in `docs/formats/bento.md`. Large imports: streaming readers, chunked import with resumable progress (plan 10).

## 7. Milestones: scope and exit criteria (plan 8 + ui 11)

"Accessibility work is continuous from M2 onward"; manual screen-reader pass per milestone (plan 5, 8).

- **M0**. Scope: decisions; legacy-format discovery; repo scaffolding; `.gitignore`; CI running offline tests. UI: copy tokens into the application stylesheet; add fonts and licences; record them in `docs/dependencies.md`.
  - [ ] ADRs accepted
  - [ ] `docs/formats/bento.md` first findings
  - [ ] Empty app serves a page
  - [ ] Empty page renders the shell in all four themes (ui 11)
  - [ ] `.gitignore` entries exist before any code that creates data: `*.db`, `*.sqlite*`, `*.tiffin`, `.env*`, `/local/`, `/data/` (CLAUDE)
- **M1**. Scope: installer, system DB, auth, roles, project create/open, schema engine, field types. UI: shell, sign-in, project list; design and build installer, people, sharing, schema editor. Also from M1: core-only operations, core authorization, trash, snapshots, audit log (plan 8).
  - [ ] Headless tests for schema and storage
  - [ ] Admin can create a project and a table
  - [ ] Screens match the mock-ups at 1360 px and 390 px (ui 11)
- **M2**. Scope: list view, auto-generated form, record CRUD, search/sort, design tokens, accessibility settings. UI: list view, record form, display settings, search results, empty and error states.
  - [ ] A Member can add, find, and edit records by keyboard only
  - [ ] Contrast tests pass
  - [ ] Token contrast tests cover all 10 theme and accent combinations (light and dark x 4 accents, plus 2 high-contrast) and reproduce the ui 4.2 figures
  - [ ] Warning token fixed (light theme `--warn` on `--warn-soft` is 6.81:1; target 7:1)
- **M3**. Scope: import/export framework; CSV and XLSX import; CSV, XLSX, JSON export; project archive. UI: import review plus the three undesigned import steps; export.
  - [ ] Round-trip tests on seeded synthetic fixtures
  - [ ] Import flow usable by keyboard only (ui 11)
- **M4**. Scope: relations UI, attachments, saved collections. UI: collection editor, relation picker, attachments, trash.
  - [ ] Linked records editable from a form
  - [ ] Attachment access control tested
  - [ ] Relation and attachment controls match the record mock-up (ui 11)
- **M5**. Scope: form editor and source editing with sanitizer. UI: form editor and source view.
  - [ ] Editor output equals hand-editable HTML
  - [ ] Sanitizer test corpus passes
  - [ ] Editor output renders correctly under every appearance setting (ui 11)
- **M6**. Scope: legacy-product import plugin. UI work: none listed.
  - [ ] Synthetic legacy-structure fixture imports with relations and attachments
  - [ ] Import report complete
- **M7**. Scope: packaging, upgrade path, host and user documentation; v1 release. UI: About page; favicon and app icon wired in.
  - [ ] Release archive installs on the reference shared host by upload and setup page only
  - [ ] Visual pass of every screen in every theme (ui 11)
- **M8 (post-v1)**. Scope: WYSIWYG form editor: drag and drop, alignment and distribution tools, static text elements, keyboard-operable; snap-to-grid CSS grid with explicit row/column positions; same form format; simple editor remains as basic mode (ADR 0006).
  - [ ] Forms round-trip between simple editor, WYSIWYG editor, and source view without loss
  - [ ] Accessibility checks pass on editor output
- **M9 (post-v1)**. Scope: MCP server with OAuth 2.1, scopes, audit log, pre-change snapshots (ADR 0005). Stateless HTTP endpoint in PHP, one JSON-RPC request per HTTP request.
  - [ ] OAuth and MCP design documents reviewed (an OAuth design document is required before implementation)
  - [ ] Conformance and abuse-case tests pass
  - [ ] Disabled by default

## 10. Dependencies named in the docs (plan 9, ADR 0007)

None added yet. Each must be recorded in `docs/dependencies.md` when added. Plan 9 states licences "from general knowledge"; all must be confirmed against each project's own licence file.

| Dependency | Purpose | Stated licence | Caveats |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenSpout | Streaming CSV/XLSX read and write | MIT | PHP 8.3 compatibility unverified; shipped in `vendor/` in the release archive |
| PHPUnit | Tests (dev only) | BSD-3-Clause | Not shipped in releases |
| Inter | Default UI typeface | OFL-1.1 (to confirm) | Font asset |
| Atkinson Hyperlegible | User option; wordmark | OFL-1.1 (to confirm) | Font asset |
| Lexend | User option | OFL-1.1 (to confirm) | Font asset |
| Source Serif 4 | User option | OFL-1.1 (to confirm) | Font asset |

Font rules: self-hosted WOFF2, Latin subsets, regular and bold only, `font-display: swap`, one font-face stylesheet per bundled face allowed, licence file shipped per family (ui 10). OFL-1.1 is approved for bundled font assets only, not code dependencies (ADR 0004, CLAUDE). Required PHP extensions: `pdo_sqlite`, `zip`, `xmlreader` (plan 10). Sanitizer library: none named. Composer is implied by `vendor/` (plan 3.2).

## 11. Repository rules that constrain implementation (CLAUDE)

- Name: "TiffinDB" always in prose, code, docs, metadata, commits; never shortened. Lower-case `tiffindb` only where a technical identifier requires it (brand README). Refer to the owner only as "the lead developer" or "the maintainer".
- Public repo. Never commit or paste into issues/PRs/commit messages: real user data, PII, personal names of real people, emails, phone numbers, addresses, account or device identifiers, credentials/keys/tokens/`.env` contents, non-public business information, exports/backups/screenshots of real databases. Never reference the maintainer's employers or affiliated organizations.
- Fixtures, samples, screenshots, doc examples: obviously synthetic ("Example Person", `user@example.com`, 192.0.2.0/24, 555-01xx), preferably generated with a documented seed; never derived from real data.
- No names or emails in `AUTHORS`, comments, docs, or sample data unless the maintainer directs it for a named file.
- If sensitive data is found in the tree or a prompt: do not copy it; stop and notify. If already committed: report; do not hide with a follow-up commit.
- `.gitignore` entries (`*.db`, `*.sqlite*`, `*.tiffin`, `.env*`, `/local/`, `/data/`) before any code that creates such files.
- Licence: `AGPL-3.0-or-later`; `LICENSE` is canonical, do not edit. Every source file carries `SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later` plus a copyright line using "TiffinDB contributors". Dependency licences allowed: MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, LGPL, MPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, AGPL-3.0 (fonts also OFL-1.1); forbidden: GPL-2.0-only, proprietary, source-available, non-commercial-restricted.
- "Source code" link reachable in the UI (footer or About).
- Do not copy code, schemas, UI assets, icons, or docs from the legacy product or any proprietary product. Do not use the name "Bento" in the product name, UI, or package metadata; "inspired by" / "a replacement for" in prose is acceptable. No code from unknown/incompatible-licence sources.
- No telemetry, analytics, or network calls without explicit maintainer approval and an opt-in design.
- Tests deterministic, offline, synthetic fixtures only. Data stored in an open documented format, exportable as CSV and JSON at minimum without the application.
- Work on the assigned branch only; no pull requests unless asked; small imperative commits; state assumptions and uncertainties in design docs and PR descriptions. Do not fabricate citations, standards, or licence text.
- No inline `style` attributes or inline scripts in application output; every screen works without JavaScript (ui 10).

## 12. Contradictions and underspecified items (flagged, not resolved)

Contradictions:

1. **Legacy product name in UI/metadata.** CLAUDE forbids the name "Bento" in the UI and package metadata, but plan 3.2 names the plugin directory `plugins/import/bento/`, plugin manifests carry an id and name shown to Admins (plan 6.2), and the import format must be labelled somehow in the UI. No doc says what the plugin id or UI label should be.
2. **Single-transaction commit vs chunked resumable import.** Plan 6.1 commits an import in a single transaction; plan 10 mitigates PHP limits with "chunked import with resumable progress". The two are not reconciled.
3. **Form sanitizer "no external URLs" vs links and images.** Plan 4 bans external URLs in stored form HTML; ADR 0006 requires the v1 format to support static images and proposes text with links. Where a static image's source may come from is not specified.
4. **Auto-generated form columns.** Plan 4 and ADR 0003 say single column; the accepted model UI shows 2 or 3 columns (ui 9.1). Unresolved, and the M1/M4 "match the mock-up" checks depend on it.
5. **Default typeface.** ADR 0004 body says Atkinson Hyperlegible is the default; superseded by ADR 0007 (Inter). Treat ADR 0007 as current; the old text remains in ADR 0004.
6. **High-contrast themes "stay black and white" (ADR 0007)** but `tokens.css` gives them non-neutral values (`.t-hcl` `--accent #003B37`, `--soft #D5F0EC`, warning colours; `.t-hcd` `--accent #8FF5E8`).
7. **Trash timing.** Trash is a core feature from M1 (plan 8) and the M2 record mock-up has "Move to trash", but the Trash and restore screen is assigned to M4 (ui 6.2, ui 11); plan 8's M4 scope does not mention trash.
8. **"No outbound network calls" (plan 7)** vs possible MCP client-registration fetch (ADR 0005); post-v1, open as plan Q4.
9. **M1 exit "screens match the mock-ups at 1360 px and 390 px"** covers a milestone where three of the five screen groups (installer, people/sharing, schema editor) have no mock-up. Likewise the Plugins screen is listed for M3 in ui 6.2 but absent from the M3 UI work in ui 11.
10. **Layer table vs features.** `core/forms` depends only on schema but binds records (records come from `core/query`); `core/auth` depends on "system DB", which is not a listed layer; `core/storage` is described only in terms of project files. Trash, snapshots, and audit log are core features with no assigned layer.
11. **Token units.** `tokens.css` defines sizes in px (`--text-base: 18px`), while ui 4.3 and the tokens file comment require `rem` for all sizes. Minor: plan 2 table lists row 15 before row 14; plan 2 row 9 lists JSON export as an aside while ADR 0004 lists it as a v1 format (same outcome).

Items that agents likely cannot complete without the maintainer:

12. M0 exit "`docs/formats/bento.md` first findings" needs real legacy files, which must never enter the repo, and the discovery output needs maintainer review before commit. M6 fixtures must reproduce the "observed structure", so M6 depends on it.
13. Plan Q2 (verify the reference host on a real account before M1) and the M7 exit (release archive installs on that host) need a real hosting account. Manual screen-reader passes per milestone (plan 5) and the M7 "visual pass" are manual checks.

Underspecified (no doc gives the answer):

14. Schemas: column lists for all `_tiffin_*` tables and the whole system database; stable key and generated identifier formats; SQLite storage column type per field type; choice options, currency, duration, auto-number, and rating storage details.
15. Trash storage mechanism, audit log location/schema/v1 events, snapshot naming/retention/restore and the list of "risky operations".
16. Relation cardinalities other than many-to-many; "referential cleanup" behaviour on delete/trash.
17. Attachment hash algorithm, size/type limits, quotas, orphan cleanup; whether WAL sidecar files affect folder-copy backup and the zip project archive (inference from plan 10 and ADR 0001; the docs do not discuss it).
18. Password reset: the sign-in mock-up has a "plain-language reset note" but no mechanism is specified (and outbound calls are banned). First-Admin creation in the installer is not described.
19. Member permissions beyond "view and edit records": creating collections, import/export (sidebar shows Import/Export/Trash to all on list view; ADR 0002 puts imports/exports under Admin), restoring from trash, deleting records.
20. Multiple forms per table: `_tiffin_forms` has a "default flag", but form selection and creation UI are not described.
21. Search semantics (plan 8 says "search/sort"; ui 6.2 adds "search results across tables"): full-text or substring, indexing, scope. Filter and collection rule operators are shown only in the mock-up ("all/any, rule rows"). Autosave is named as a JS enhancement (plan 4, ui 10) with no behaviour defined. List paging size not specified.
22. Exact CSP, session lifetime, login throttling, password rules; sanitizer allowlist contents; form format version scheme; JSON export schema; plugin manifest file name and format; `Importer`/`Exporter` method signatures beyond `inspect()` and `read()`.
23. CI system and test layout: "CI running offline tests" only. PHP coding standard, autoloading, routing scheme, URL structure: not specified. Upgrade path (M7) for the application and system database: only project-file migrations are described. Project archive import: how ids, grants, and conflicts are handled is not specified.
24. M6, M8, M9 have no UI work or UI exit checks in ui 11.
